stages.name: Observe
stages.instruction: Drag the sliders to set amplitude $X_m$, angular frequency $\omega$, and phase $\varphi$, then press PLAY. Watch how $x(t) = X_m \cos(\omega t + \varphi)$ shapes the bob's back-and-forth motion.
stages.concept: Rectilinear sinusoidal motion: $x(t) = X_m \cos(\omega t + \varphi)$. Period $T = \dfrac{2\pi}{\omega}$. Amplitude $X_m$ is the maximum elongation; $\varphi$ shifts the whole curve horizontally.

stages.name: Experiment
stages.instruction: Match the ghost bob. Tune $X_m$, $\omega$, $\varphi$ so your bob (orange) tracks the target ghost (teal) for a full period. The waveform overlay shows both curves — line them up.
stages.concept: Two sinusoidal motions coincide when they share $X_m$, $\omega$ (or equivalently $T = 2\pi/\omega$), and $\varphi$. A phase advance of $\varphi$ shifts $x(t)$ leftward by $\varphi / \omega$ seconds.

stages.name: Evaluate
stages.instruction: No waveform. Read the target's $X_m$, $T$, $\varphi$, compute $\omega = 2\pi / T$ on paper, set your sliders, then PLAY. One attempt per target — no spray-and-pray.
stages.concept: From $T$: $\omega = \dfrac{2\pi}{T}$. From an initial elongation $x_0 = X_m \cos\varphi$ at $t=0$: $\varphi = \arccos(x_0 / X_m)$. The sign of the initial velocity picks the correct branch.

labels.tip1: move each slider, press PLAY, then observe
labels.tip2: align your bob (orange) with the ghost (teal)
labels.tip3: compute ω = 2π/T from the target, set sliders, then PLAY
labels.peek_tip_period: T and ω are locked together: ω = 2π/T. Shorter T means a faster oscillation (larger ω).
labels.peek_tip_phase: At t = 0 the bob sits at x₀ = Xm·cos(φ). Read the target's starting position to pin down φ.
labels.peek_tip_amplitude: Xm is the maximum |x| reached — it does not depend on ω or φ. Set it before tuning the others.

1.1: The three sliders control amplitude Xm (m), angular frequency ω (rad/s), and phase φ (rad).
1.2: Press PLAY to start the animation. The bob slides along the track; the waveform on the right shows x(t).
1.3: Try large vs small ω to see the period shrink or grow. T = 2π/ω.

2.1: The teal ghost bob follows the target motion. Your orange bob follows your slider settings.
2.2: Match Xm first (both bobs should reach the same extremes), then ω (same period), then φ (both at the same position at t = 0).
2.3: The waveform overlay shows both curves. Two identical sinusoids overlap perfectly.

3.1: The target's Xm, T, φ are labeled next to the ghost. Compute ω = 2π/T from T.
3.2: Set Xm to the labeled amplitude. Set ω = 2π/T. Set φ to the labeled phase (radians).
3.3: One attempt per target. Verify your slider readings match the labels before pressing PLAY.
